character.lede: A single-storey cottage on a raised floor has a steep brown side gable with two brick dormers and a grey brick chimney. An open walnut living, dining and kitchen room leads to one long whitewashed family bedroom.

spots.line: A breakfast bar and a coffee maker sit in the open kitchen.
A family bed and a loft bed share the long bedroom.
A play tent, a kids' table and building blocks fill the kids' zone.

facts.style: Single-storey cottage on a raised floor: a steep brown side gable with two brick dormers and a grey brick chimney, twin front-gabled glass wings (grey and red-brown brick) flanking a painted recessed entry in a black frame with a glazed French pair, open walnut living-dining-kitchen, one long whitewashed family bedroom with a kids' zone, a spindle-railed back porch and a privacy-fenced garden

character.truths: The Core sits on a desk in the Family Bedroom, in sight of the door. There is a television in the Living Room. A small single-storey cottage: the kitchen, dining and living room are one open space. Picnic table and loungers outside.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

yuvomi: [note] Stored in SQLite on your Core. CalDAV and CardDAV sync are optional.
one household planner, not an account per person
already in the persona pool: share cap risk
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
bentopdf: Dual licence: AGPL-3.0 or paid commercial; fine for household use
Listing says "nothing to leak": drop that wording
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
kiwix: marketplace: Ships with an empty library: the compose runs kiwix-serve on /data/library.xml with no content and no way in the Hub to add or register ZIM files; the QA capture shows "No result".
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
pi-hole: [claims] Network-wide blocking at DNS. Do not call it parental control or promise safety.
Blocks ad, tracker and bad domains at DNS: not parental control and no promise of safety
Unblocked lookups are forwarded to an upstream resolver (the upstream demo dashboard lists a public DNS, dns.google), so a DNS provider still sees them and it is not offline
Overlaps AdGuard Home: one per household
jellyfin: [note] Plays your own files. Say that, not "Netflix".
[claims] Do not say it plays copyrighted material from anywhere.
Plays your own media only: never "streams any movie".
QA capture is the setup wizard with a container id as the server name; the gallery frame is a demo library with lurid exploitation film posters: neither usable.
mealie: [note] Pasting a recipe URL fetches that web page. Everything it saves stays on your Core.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pasting a URL fetches that web page
vaultwarden: [note] Bitwarden-compatible server, unofficial. Do not say "Bitwarden".
donetick: [cloud-link] Notifications use Telegram or Pushover. Both are outside services.
NFC-tag completion needs a phone that reads NFC on the home network
hortusfox: Do not say it keeps plants alive
Plant health alerts and a public gallery exist: keep the gallery off in a story
listmonk: [cloud-link] Sending at volume needs an SMTP provider or mail server. Do not promise delivery.
docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
blinko: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
AI search and chat need a model provider added in the app (OpenAI, Ollama, LiteLLM...): not wired by the Hub.
No QA run; gallery frame is upstream marketing with a "#Password" tagged note and a gmail file name: reject.
Companion desktop and mobile clients are separate downloads.
mstream: Description says "from anywhere", "completely private" and "no data collection": absolute and remote claims, paraphrase
kokoro: [note] OpenAI-compatible speech API. No GPU requirement in the listing.
OpenAI-compatible speech API; web player included.
No GPU requirement in the listing; no speed claim.
Capture is real (FastKoko player) on a dark purple background.
librespeed: Say "the link to the Core" or "the Wi-Fi in this room"; never "internet speed"
No speed figures in copy (num rules): show the act, not a number
Listing says "privacy-focused" and "no tracking": do not repeat
searxng: [cloud-link] It queries outside search engines for you. Say "private search", not "offline search".
cloud-link: the engines still see the query from the Core
listing says users are not tracked: do not repeat
endurain: [cloud-link] Optional sync with Strava and Garmin Connect. Bulk GPX and FIT upload is local.
Strava and Garmin sync are outside links: say bulk upload is the local path
GPS history is location data: story must not map a home address
linkwarden: Sharing links publicly needs inbound reach: keep the story to saving, not sharing
The Pocket name in replaces is stale
drawio: Stateless: diagrams live in the browser or as .drawio files on the person's own device. The Core serves the editor only, so never say the diagram sits on the Core.
Listing says nothing else phones home: leave it.
QA screenshot is a blank editor.
firefly-iii: [cloud-link] Bank import through GoCardless or Spectre is an outside service. CSV import stays local.
[claims] Bookkeeping tool. No financial advice and no savings promises.
marketplace: Replaces lists Mint, which Intuit retired in 2024.

caveats: Say "the link to the Core" or "the Wi-Fi in this room"; never "internet speed"
No speed figures in copy (num rules): show the act, not a number
Listing says "privacy-focused" and "no tracking": do not repeat
